coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: MB360 (701 China Basin St)
record.summary: MB360 is a residential building at 701 China Basin St (188 units per the DataSF Assessor roll), part of a two-block (Block 5 and Block 11) Mission Bay apartment development originally built by BRE Properties (now Essex Property Trust), with MVE + Partners as prime architect. The architect's project page gives different unit counts (Block 5 = 170, Block 11 = 190) and does not say which block is 701 China Basin St. DataSF Assessor records give 2016 as this parcel's year built, and the architect's project page gives 'Completion 2016' for the development.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL lot geometry -- the outline is Assessor lot 8710009 (7,659 m2, active), so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a surveyed building footprint: it includes any yard, setback or plaza inside the lot and can sit a little off the walls. Until 2026-10-12 this record showed the surveyed building footprint (DataSF Building Footprints (mblr SF8710009)); 96% of that outline lies inside the lot and it covered 70% of the lot.

milestones.text: BRE Properties' ~360-unit MB360 development (Blocks 5 and 11 of Mission Bay, per the architect's project page) is reported to have begun vertical construction. The Registry, published May 1, 2013, says BRE "has begun vertical construction on its 360-unit MB360 apartment development"; that is an announcement, so the start date itself is not known and only the year is shown (SFGate, March 2014: "Construction began last year" on the building that burned)

open_questions: Apartment-listing aggregators (Apartments.com, Redfin, ApartmentHomeLiving, among others) give 2014 as this block's construction year, but DataSF Assessor records and the project architect's own project page both give 2016; not resolved which reflects actual first occupancy versus an earlier leasing target that slipped.

Contemporaneous press (SFGate, CBS News San Francisco) reported a 5-alarm fire on March 11, 2014 that destroyed an under-construction MB360 building (CBS News, May 7, 2014: "a 172-unit building was being built as part of the MB360 development project ... The unfinished building was destroyed and demolished in the days following the massive blaze"); no source read says the building was rebuilt; no source found specifies which of the two street addresses (701 China Basin St, this record, vs. 1200 4th St) was the one destroyed, so it is not asserted here which block the fire affected.
Precise month of this block's actual completion/first occupancy is not sourced beyond the bare Assessor year.
Developer of record beyond BRE Properties/Essex Property Trust, and any subsequent sale history: not yet researched.

The Registry's own article (already cited above) reports that BRE Properties "expects total development cost of $227 million, or $630,000 a unit" (an expected figure, May 2013, not a final cost) -- but that figure covers the whole 360-unit MB360 development, which the architect's page describes as two blocks (this record's 701 China Basin St block plus the separate 1200 4th St block) as one project, not this 188-unit block alone. No block-specific figure was found, so no record-scope figure is added here.

The Apartments.com listing could not be checked on 2026-09-29; an archived copy exists at web.archive.org/web/20211031174227/https://www.apartments.com/mb360-san-francisco-ca/bzdysc8/ (not checked). The 701 China Basin St address is confirmed by the Assessor and OpenStreetMap.

Unit count: the Assessor roll gives 188 units for 701 China Basin St. The architect's project page cited here (Ignition Architecture, which designed two of the five buildings on Block 5) lists "Units 362 total; Block 5 = 170 / ...; Block 11 = 190 / ..." (its own per-block figures add to 360, not 362) and no street addresses; the page of the project's other architect, MVE + Partners, could not be read on 2026-10-12. A 2014 CurbedSF report quoted by LocalWiki gives 172 units for the destroyed building and 188 for the other, which is not tied here to a street address.
